newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA FUEL OIL - STEADY DESPITE LARGE STOCK BUILD.
newsitem.headline: ASIA FUEL OIL - STEADY DESPITE LARGE STOCK BUILD.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was steady in quiet trading with the market supported by firmer swap values although sentiment was slightly shaken by the increase in stocks, traders said on Thursday.
Traders said the 1.363 million barrel build in residual fuel oil stocks to 11.53 million for the week ending August 13 placed the brakes on the recent fuel oil rally.
"The stocks did affect sentiment a bit, but the absence of physical bid and offers has made people a bit jittery. You are are not sure how long it (rally) is going to last," one trader said.
Traders said the rise in stocks was due to the arrival of several fuel oil cargoes from the Middle East--all of which are already committed.
But despite this, the build in stocks did make players re-think about the lastest rally where swap prices have put on about $2.50 per tonne since Monday.
September swaps peaked to trade at $105.25 before coming under selling pressure as sellers came out to take profits.
"The $105.00 resistance mark is not easy to break. A lot of people came out to take profit at around this level," one trader said.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $104.50/$105.00 per tonne, up from Wednesday's $104.00/$105.00, brokers said.
But the lastest level is well below the traded highs of $105.00 and $105.25 done this morning, they said.
The higher stocks and absence of physical bids/offers also led to agressively selling on the bunker market where sellers were also of the opinion that the market might have peaked.
A major sold a total of 4,000 tonnes of 380-cst at $106.00 per tonne, traders said.
